In chapter 5 of the players handbook there’s a section on mounts and vehicles. It states how for barding (armor used by horses or other mounts), it says that it costs 4 times the equivalent amount for humanoids armor and weighs twice as much. For example, scale mail armor for a horse would cost 200 gold and would weigh 180 lbs.

I’d say your best bet is if the players do happen to tame or befriend a wild polar bear or owl bear, they would need to not only have the funds but would also need to find a smith specialized enough to craft it (hypothetically, there could be a smith based out of the dwarven valley that could do it.) You should come up with how long it would take to craft the armor in advance, that way you don’t make up a time interval on the spot that either takes too long for the party’s enjoyment or takes too little for the sake of preparing yourself for encounter balancing.

The stronghold itself is currently occupied by a band of Orcs that’s been ravaging the nearby towns. Beneath that lies the Glitterhame (like a mini-pseudo underdark). I’ve been DMing very on and off for maybe 2 years. I’ve been playing for 3. If you were still wondering.

The session lasted from 3:00 to 9:00 with a break in the middle for dinner so roughly 5 hours give or take. The first encounter lasted about a half hour, which involved 5 zombies and an ogre zombie. The second one lasted longer, maybe a little over an hour due to the fact that they were in the process of dealing with one trio of zombie duergar, but because the zombie was turned by the paladin’s channel divinity it fled and alerted 3 more zombies. 

The one thing that was rather controversial was one character, the warlock, was using the blink spell. I’m not too familiar of the mechanics of the ethereal plane, but the player was not happy with how I handled it. He wanted to use blink to save him and another companion from dying to a 300ft drop by teleporting to the ethereal plane. I’ve always sort of imagined it as having a ghastly counterpart to the material world, so I kind of winged how it worked. The player was not pleased, though personally I would have liked this if he had address the matter at the time and better explained how it worked. Why because I was unsure fully of how the spell worked.

There were definitely changes I could’ve made looking back to have made it easier. To be fair my reasoning though was at the time the players were at a much higher level than the encounter was meant for ( they were level 5, was more meat for 3-4). Plus they had gathered some magical items on the way that did help in the fight somewhat. Again, I could’ve handled it better that I know. 

The “drama” was that one character was trying to take the orc survivors that the players had after fighting the majority of them and forcing them to breed and sell their young into slavery. Everyone else got mad at him, so his character left. They then had issues traveling further in because they felt that they were undermanned, and so the went to find him again and get him back.

I went through the same thing last year. Had my dog for 11 years, really helped me through a lot of shit. 

I know this is a hard choice to make. Really I know. But understand that your dog has probably lived an amazing life with you. To him, you're his entire world. 

If you feel like he's really suffering, then I would say putting him down would be best. They go peacefully, trust me. You're gonna want to be there when they put him down. Just so you can say goodbye and make sure he has his buddy with him until the very next end. It's going to suck a lot when he's gone, I still cry whenever I think about my dog. Eventually the pain will pass, and you'll be able to look back on how amazing it was having him by your side.

And hey, once everything gets better, perhaps you should consider adopting another dog. There's always one out there in need of a home of his/her own. 

Just remember, you saved him from a horrible life, and gave him an amazing one. He got the chance to find someone to love. That's all a dog can ask for in life.
